item.title: Tambuwal dismisses APC defection rumours
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO: Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he plans to defect from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the claims as false and misleading. The former Sokoto State governor, through his media office, said he had no intention of leaving the ADC, warning that the speculation could create unnecessary confusion ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement dated October 19, 2026, and signed by Prince Daniel, Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to the senator, Tambuwal’s media office reaffirmed his commitment to the ADC and its political objectives. “For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Tambuwal has no plans to join the APC. Suggestions to the contrary are false, baseless and should be disregarded,” the statement said. The clarification comes amid heightened political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 elections, as parties and their leading figures position themselves for the contest. However, the media office insisted that the reports should not be interpreted as an indication of any impending change in Tambuwal’s party affiliation. It explained that the senator’s longstanding relationships with politicians across party lines should not be misconstrued as evidence of a planned defection, noting that his years in public service had enabled him to maintain friendships and political contacts beyond the ADC. The statement also cautioned against drawing conclusions from photographs and video clips circulating on social media, stressing that cordial interactions between politicians from different parties did not necessarily indicate negotiations to change political allegiance. “Political civility is no proof of political realignment,” it said, adding that exchanging greetings or interacting with members of another party should not be presented as evidence of a defection plan. item.title: Governance will suffer if Tinubu campaigns nationwide — Ex-Obidient Chief
item.description: …Challenges critics to debate fuel subsidy removal By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Director-General of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance, also known as the Tinubu Must Stay (TMS) Movement, Marcel Ngogbehei, has said governance could suffer if President Bola Tinubu personally campaigns across all 36 states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient Movement, also challenged critics of the removal of the petrol subsidy to an open debate on the policy, urging them to offer alternatives that take Nigeria’s economic realities into account. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja alongside the National Coordinator of the movement, Engr. Ibrahim Said Uba, during a media parley where he explained why the President might not personally attend campaign activities in every state. “One of the greatest challenges we are having in this country is the time to govern and the time to do electioneering,” Ngogbehei said. He said participants should examine the challenges the policy was intended to address and assess whether alternative approaches could deliver better outcomes. “We are telling the person, let us sit down and let us x-ray these things. “You need to first of all show us that you understand the problem and then, if you were there, what would you do differently, putting into consideration all the complexities of Nigeria?” he asked. He said Nigerians had been warned that maintaining the policy could eventually undermine the government’s ability to meet obligations, including the payment of salaries. item.title: Abiodun mourns Fasoranti, describes him as democratic icon
item.description: Gov. Dapo Abiodun of Ogun has expressed sorrow over the death of elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing it as a monumental loss to Nigeria. In a statement on Tuesday in Abeokuta, Abiodun, Chairman of the Southern Governors’ Forum, conveyed his condolences to Afenifere, Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo, Yoruba leaders, and the deceased’s family and associates. The governor described Fasoranti, who recently celebrated his 100th birthday, as a patriot whose life was defined by service and commitment to the advancement of the Yoruba nation and Nigeria. He said the late elder statesman was among the enduring voices in Nigeria’s democratic struggle, whose courage and sacrifices helped shape the country’s political development. Abiodun noted that Fasoranti played a significant role in the struggle for democracy, particularly during military rule, earning recognition as a defender of democratic governance and constitutional rule. He said the deceased remained steadfast in advocating justice, equity, good governance and restructuring, demonstrating his commitment to building a united and prosperous Nigeria. The governor described Fasoranti as one of the surviving links to a generation of nationalist leaders who confronted authoritarianism and championed democratic freedoms. “The elder statesman’s death has created a significant vacuum in the Yoruba socio-political landscape; his contributions to national development remains indelible. “Fasoranti’s legacy will endure through the values he upheld, the causes he championed, and the generations of Nigerians inspired by his commitment to democracy,” he said. He urged Afenifere, the people of Ondo, the Yoruba nation and the deceased’s family to take solace in his remarkable life and contributions to society. item.title: Why I rejected Real Madrid, Inter Milan, Bayern Munich — Gerrard
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard has revealed why he turned down interest from European giants Real Madrid, Inter Milan and Bayern Munich, insisting he has no regrets about remaining at Anfield during his playing career. As reported by ESPN, Gerrard disclosed his decision while speaking on the Overlap Daily podcast, explaining that he was never keen on leaving Liverpool despite interest from some of Europe’s biggest clubs. “I had some interest from foreign teams and the majority of that was through [now Real Madrid coach] José Mourinho,” Gerrard said. “Inter Milan, Real Madrid, on a couple of occasions, and at the back end a few conversations with my agent when [Bastian] Schweinsteiger was leaving Bayern [in 2015].” The former England captain said he was content at Liverpool, particularly during Brendan Rodgers’ time as manager, and had little interest in pursuing a move abroad. “I wasn’t really that interested in it because I was never going to leave Liverpool at the time. I was enjoying my football under [coach] Brendan [Rodgers] when that one came but yes, three or four of the big teams showed some interest during my career, which is flattering, of course it is,” he added. Gerrard, who made 710 appearances for Liverpool and won nine trophies during his 19-year playing career, admitted that watching English players such as Jude Bellingham at Real Madrid and Harry Kane at Bayern Munich enjoy success abroad sometimes makes him reflect on what might have happened had he left Anfield. “When you watch the likes of Jude Bellingham [at Real Madrid] and Harry Kane [at Bayern Munich] and you see them winning loads of trophies with foreign teams, it does cross your mind and you go back and you think,” he said. “But I have no regrets in terms of the decisions I made. No regrets.” Gerrard retired from international football in 2014 and ended his playing career in 2016 after a spell with Major League Soccer side LA Galaxy, having joined the American club in 2015. He subsequently moved into management, taking charge of Rangers and Aston Villa before managing Saudi Pro League side Al Ettifaq. He has been without a club since leaving the Saudi Arabian side in January 2025. item.title: Reps probe SGF’s approval for lawmakers’ foreign trips
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has mandated its Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate a circular requiring the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) to approve official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. The House also reaffirmed the constitutional independence of the legislature, warning that subjecting lawmakers’ official foreign travel to executive approval could undermine the principle of separation of powers. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi, who drew the House’s attention to a circular dated August 13, 2026, with reference number PRS59648/5.13/TI/335, issued by the Office of the SGF. The circular reportedly requires prior approval from the SGF before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs can issue Notes Verbales for official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. Moving the motion, Onuakalusi expressed concern that the requirement could compromise legislative independence, impede parliamentary diplomacy and create an inappropriate system of executive control over the legislature. He maintained that the National Assembly was an independent arm of government, not a ministry, department, agency or subordinate institution of the executive. The lawmaker cited Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which establish the legislature, executive and judiciary as distinct arms of government founded on the principles of separation of powers and checks and balances. He also referenced Section 51 of the Constitution and Section 22 of the National Assembly Act, 2014, in reaffirming the legislature’s constitutional status and authority over its internal administrative arrangements. Onuakalusi stressed that executive administrative procedures must respect constitutional boundaries and should not interfere with the legislature’s ability to discharge its constitutional responsibilities. Following the adoption of the motion, the House directed the Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate the circular and its implications for parliamentary independence. The committees are expected to recommend appropriate legislative action and report back to the House within four weeks for further consideration. The resolution reinforces the House’s position that administrative procedures introduced by the executive must not undermine the autonomy of the National Assembly or interfere with its constitutional functions. Bill, 2026, warning that the legislation could create regulatory conflicts, duplicate existing laws and disrupt legitimate businesses. NECA, in a formal submission to the Senate Committee on Health, urged the National Assembly to exclude tobacco products from the proposed legislation, arguing that the sector is already subject to a dedicated regulatory framework. The Bill, sponsored by Senator Umar Sadiq Suleiman, passed second reading in the Senate on July 21, 2026. It seeks to repeal the Food, Drugs and Related Products Act, 2004, and establish a new regulatory framework for food, medical and related products. However, NECA argued that extending the Bill’s provisions to tobacco products could conflict with the National Tobacco Control Act, 2015, the National Tobacco Control Regulations, 2019, and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria Act, 2015. According to the employers’ association, the proposed framework could create overlapping responsibilities among the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, SON and the Nigeria Customs Service. It warned that such overlaps could lead to multiple product-registration requirements, duplicated approvals, conflicting enforcement decisions, increased compliance costs and uncertainty for businesses. NECA maintained that tobacco products constitute a distinct regulatory category and should not be treated as food or medicines under the proposed law. It also argued that NAFDAC’s existing statutory mandate does not expressly cover tobacco products, adding that their inclusion in the Bill could extend the agency’s authority into an area already governed by dedicated legislation. The association further raised concerns about provisions granting additional powers over product registration, suspension, seizure, factory operations and enforcement, warning that these could conflict with the responsibilities of existing regulatory institutions. Of particular concern to NECA is the proposed ceiling-list mechanism, which it said could give NAFDAC excessive administrative discretion to restrict products without adequate statutory safeguards and oversight. The association called on lawmakers to introduce safeguards against unilateral regulatory decisions, strengthen coordination among existing institutions and amend the Bill to prevent duplication, regulatory uncertainty and unnecessary disruption to businesses. It stressed that a coherent regulatory environment was essential for investment, economic growth, effective public-health protection and compliance with the law. NECA also urged lawmakers to ensure that the proposed legislation complemented, rather than contradicted, Nigeria’s existing tobacco-control framework. The association said effective regulation should be based on clearly defined institutional responsibilities, predictable compliance requirements, proportionate enforcement and coordination among relevant government agencies. It expressed readiness to engage further with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to achieve a legislative outcome that protects public health while sustaining regulatory certainty and business confidence. Health Ministry, SON seek deferment The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare also expressed reservations about the proposed amendments at a public hearing on the Bill. Represented by Dr Adebisi Adegoke, mni, Director of Hospital Services, the Ministry raised concerns about potential regulatory conflicts, duplication and overlapping mandates, which it said could undermine effective government administration. It recommended deferring consideration of the Bill to allow further consultations among affected stakeholders and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s existing responsibilities. SON similarly raised concerns that some provisions of the proposed legislation conflicted with the law establishing the organisation and could interfere with its statutory responsibilities. The standards body backed the call for the Bill’s consideration to be deferred, arguing that a more comprehensive review was needed to remove unnecessary complexities and overlapping mandates. It also expressed concern that the process leading to the proposed amendments had not involved sufficient engagement and consultation with affected institutions. Industry operators warn of business disruption Tobacco industry operators have also expressed reservations about the proposed legislation, warning that another layer of regulation could complicate compliance rather than improve regulatory effectiveness. At a recent public hearing, industry stakeholders argued that tobacco manufacturing, importation, distribution, packaging, health warnings, product standards and related activities were already subject to extensive statutory controls. They warned that parallel approval and enforcement structures could expose manufacturers and importers to conflicting directives, additional administrative costs, operational disruptions and uncertainty over which regulator has final authority. The operators maintained that their concerns were not about resisting public-health regulation but about the risks of multiplying regulatory requirements without clearly demonstrated public-policy benefits. They further argued that unpredictable compliance obligations could weaken investor confidence, discourage business expansion and complicate efforts by the Federal Government to improve Nigeria’s competitiveness and ease of doing business. item.title: Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill has concluded the drafting phase of its assignment and formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), alongside 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative review and validation. The submission was made on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation, AGF and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan. This was revealed via a statement issued by the Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila. Gbajabiamila, who was a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, explained that the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws. According to the statement: “The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate. “The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.” He further said: “The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly. “The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.” The post Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry appeared first on Vanguard News .

He expressed optimism about Nigeria’s future, citing the resilience and creativity of its people, particularly young Nigerians, whom he said needed opportunities to work, innovate and prosper. He said, “One major obstacle to Nigeria’s political development is division along ethnic, religious and regional lines. We must rise above these differences and promote politics founded on competence, Integrity, inclusion and national interest. “Nigeria must always be greater than any political party, individual or sectional interest.” The former President who served as deputy governor and governor of Bayelsa State before becoming vice-president and president of the country noted that his experience had taught him the importance of consultation, teamwork and strong institutions, just as he urged former deputy governors to promote cordial relationships between serving governors and their deputies, mentor younger politicians and discourage divisive politics. Jonathan said, “As a former deputy governor and governor of Bayelsa State before becoming vice president and subsequently president of Nigeria, I understand the opportunities and challenges associated with the office of deputy governor. “The experience teaches patience, loyalty, consultation and teamwork. Above all, it reminds us that governance is not about one individual but about strong institutions and service to the people.” Earlier in his remarks, the National Chairman of the Forum of Former Deputy Governors of Nigeria (FFDGN), Dr Chris Alozie Akomas challenged political leaders to abandon arrogance and embrace accountability, warning that power without character is destructive and governance without empathy is empty. Akomas who identified the widening gap between political leaders and citizens as a major obstacle to Nigeria’s development, said sustainable development could not be achieved through policies, budgets and administrative reforms alone without a fundamental change in the attitudes, values and conduct of those entrusted with public responsibility. According to Akomas, the disconnect between leaders and the people they govern has spread across government institutions, communities and families, weakening the collective effort needed to build a prosperous nation. “We cannot build a lasting future on a foundation of indifference,” he said. item.title: NYSC kidnapping: Identities of suspects vindicate us – IPOB
item.description: …Raise questions over profiling of Igbo youths …Group demands investigation into alleged sponsors of insecurity in South-East By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has called for a thorough investigation into the abduction of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State, following the arraignment of five suspects over the incident. The group said the suspects’ identities raised questions about the attribution of kidnappings and other criminal activities in the South-East to its members and the Eastern Security Network (ESN) before investigations establish those responsible. The suspects were identified as Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu, Mohammed Ali, Aminu Haliru and Ibrahim Jiji. In a statement issued on Tuesday by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emma Powerful, IPOB said the case reinforced its longstanding position that its members and ESN had been wrongly blamed for insecurity in the region. The group argued that, had the suspects not been apprehended, Igbo youths and ESN members might have been accused of the crime, potentially exposing innocent people to arrest and other alleged mistreatment. “Had this atrocious kidnapping happened without these suspects being caught, who would the Nigerian security apparatus and hostile media have blamed?” IPOB asked. The group said previous incidents in the South-East had similarly been attributed to IPOB and ESN, insisting that criminal allegations should be subjected to evidence-based investigations. IPOB maintained that its members were not responsible for kidnappings in the region, adding that ESN was established to protect communities, farmers and residents against armed attacks. The group commended the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in Imo State and the prosecuting team, describing the case as an opportunity to establish the facts surrounding the abduction. It called for a comprehensive investigation into the suspects’ identities, origins, networks and alleged accomplices, urging authorities to make the findings public in accordance with the law. IPOB also urged security agencies to investigate criminal activities based on evidence rather than ethnicity, political affiliation or unverified allegations. The statement renewed the group’s criticism of the continued detention of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, arguing that his warnings about security threats in the region had not received adequate attention. IPOB further called on South-East governors and political leaders to strengthen security in rural communities and forests, protect lives and property, and ensure that innocent residents were not unfairly associated with criminal activities. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, for consideration and approval. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services alongside the Federal Police Service as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. Presenting the committee’s report, its chairman and member representing Qua’an-Pan South Constituency, Theodore Maiyaki, said the proposed amendment was necessary in view of prevailing security challenges, manpower shortages in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen policing at the grassroots. He explained that the proposal would establish a framework for federal and state policing, with safeguards for human rights, operational standards, accountability and coordination. The committee also noted that improved security was critical to the socioeconomic development of Plateau State and the country at large, recommending that the House support the proposed constitutional alteration. Following deliberations, lawmakers adopted the recommendations and voted in support of the proposed amendment. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, commended the committee for its work and thanked members for their patience, commitment and sacrifice in considering the legislative proposal. The constitutional amendment requires approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly before it can proceed to the next stage of the process. Meanwhile, the House passed two other bills for first reading: the Plateau State Right of Patients and Medical Institutions Bill and the Plateau State Bill on Jungle Justice, Mob Action and Other Forms of Unlawful Violence Against Persons. The bills will undergo further legislative consideration in line with the rules of the Assembly. The House subsequently resolved to proceed on recess from Monday, October 19, to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, to allow members to rest and prepare for upcoming legislative responsibilities. The Speaker appreciated lawmakers, supporting staff, and other personnel for their dedication to the service of Plateau State, noting that the Assembly had continued its legislative duties beyond the initially scheduled recess period.
